title: PM to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on 25 October
subtitle:
PM to Inaugurate New Garment Manufacturing Facility in Varanasi

Women-Led Manufacturing Initiative Connects Varanasi to Global Markets

PM to witness Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi

Programme to commemorate 94th anniversary of Indian Air Force to be held under the theme “Wings over Ganges”

PM to inaugurate RBI’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 12:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on 25 October 2026. At around 11 AM, Prime Minister will inaugurate a new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi. At around 1 PM, he will witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi as the Chief Guest.
Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Odisha, where at around 4:45 PM, he will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
PM in Varanasi
Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited’s new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. The facility marks an important step towards strengthening India’s textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promoting industrial growth in the region.
Focusing on modern manufacturing practices, the facility will create meaningful employment opportunities, particularly for women, and contribute to the region’s economic progress. The inauguration also highlights Uttar Pradesh’s growing role as a destination for industrial investment and manufacturing-led growth.  With a global customer base, it is a testament to how products manufactured in Varanasi will reach across the world. Being a predominantly women-led initiative, it is a powerful symbol of women-led development.
Prime Minister will witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi. The programme will commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force and will be held under the theme “Wings over Ganges”.
The aerial display will feature aircraft including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, along with transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness in operations. The Indian Air Force’s premier display teams, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will also participate in the event. The display will showcase precision flying, coordination and operational excellence.
PM in Bhubaneswar
Marking a significant milestone in strengthening the technological foundations of India’s financial system, Prime Minister will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.  They have been designed to meet the Bank's computing requirements and to provide a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the Bank and the broader financial sector.
Four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical Payment and Settlement systems, along with other flagship initiatives. The facility has been certified to Uptime Institute Tier IV standard - the global benchmark for data centre infrastructure - placing it in the highest tier of operational resilience. It is among the largest Tier IV certified facilities in the BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance) sector worldwide. It will contribute to widening the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services, and will form the secure digital foundation on which India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy can grow. It will also help strengthen Reserve Bank’s unique standing as a leader in digital infrastructure amongst the central banking community.
The Cyber Security Training Institute will boost capability building, providing a dedicated institutional platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research, and sector-wide capability development. This institute will focus on cutting edge technologies relevant to the BFSI sector including Quantum Computing, Artificial Intelligence and other frontier technologies.

title: 11 Crore Farmer IDs Created Five Months Ahead of Schedule, Marking Major Milestone in Digital Agriculture: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
subtitle:
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan says unique digital identities will ensure transparent and faster access to government schemes, bank loans, crop insurance and disaster relief

Digital Agriculture Mission advances PM Modi’s vision of a prosperous farming sector and a developed India

Verified farmer database to improve transparency, curb duplication and ensure benefits reach eligible farmers directly
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major milestone for digital agriculture, the Government of India has achieved its target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs, five months ahead of the March 31, 2027 deadline. Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, described the achievement as a significant step towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a developed India with prosperous farmers. The milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The Farmer ID initiative is designed to provide farmers with a unique digital identity, enabling transparent, efficient and timely access to government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief, while reducing paperwork and repeated verification.
Target achieved five months ahead of schedule
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the creation of 11 crore Farmer IDs was successfully completed by the night of October 23. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had set March 31, 2027, as the deadline for achieving this target. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, state governments and field-level officials worked in coordination to achieve it five months ahead of schedule. He congratulated farmers across the country on the achievement, describing the Farmer ID as their own digital identity and an important step towards making agriculture more efficient, transparent and prosperous through modern technology.
Reduced paperwork and more transparent delivery of benefits
Shri Chouhan said the Farmer ID system would significantly reduce the need for farmers to repeatedly visit government offices and banks or submit the same documents for different schemes. Earlier, farmers often had to provide documents repeatedly to access various benefits, resulting in a loss of both time and money. With Farmer IDs, access to several key services is expected to become simpler and more transparent.
Bank loans and Kisan Credit Card: The loan process will become easier, reducing the need for repeated document verification.
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana: In the event of natural disasters or crop losses, the assessment of compensation and its disbursement will be carried out through a more transparent process, with payments made directly into farmers’ bank accounts.
Disaster relief assistance: Relief during emergencies will reach genuine and eligible farmers more quickly.
Crop procurement at Minimum Support Price (MSP): The digital system will help eliminate the role of intermediaries in the procurement process and ensure that farmers receive the full value due for their produce.
The initiative is intended to strengthen transparency and accountability in agricultural service delivery, ensuring that eligible farmers can access government support with fewer procedural hurdles.
More than 6 crore farmers have already received benefits
The Digital Agriculture Mission was launched following the Union Cabinet’s approval on September 2, 2024. The Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) being developed under the mission is already showing results on the ground. Through the Farmer ID-based service delivery system, more than 6 crore farmers across the country have so far received direct benefits under various schemes. Linking a verified farmer database with agricultural services is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification. It has also improved coordination among government departments and strengthened policy formulation and the monitoring of schemes, making it easier to track their implementation and delivery of benefits.
A strong example of cooperative federalism
Shri Chouhan credited the achievement to the collective efforts of the Central and state governments, calling it an outstanding example of cooperative federalism. He congratulated and thanked officials of the Central Government, state governments, Union Territory administrations, district-level teams and field personnel working across villages for their contribution to achieving the target ahead of schedule. States and Union Territories are also taking specific steps, in accordance with applicable rules, to bring tenant farmers and actual cultivators onto the digital platform. The objective is to ensure that no eligible farmer is left out of the government’s welfare and support programmes.
Technology to transform Indian agriculture
The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare remains committed to strengthening the Farmer Registry in line with the principle of Minimum Government, Maximum Governance. Farmer ID is not just a digital identity document; it is a strong foundation for a transparent, accountable and farmer-centric system of governance. By creating a verified digital identity for farmers, the initiative aims to improve the delivery of agricultural services and ensure that government support reaches the intended beneficiaries efficiently. Congratulating farmers across the country, Shri Chouhan urged them to embrace modern technology, avail themselves of the schemes and benefits they are entitled to without unnecessary difficulties, and contribute to taking Indian agriculture to new heights. He said the achievement marked an important step towards building a modern agricultural ecosystem in which technology serves farmers’ interests and supports the vision of a developed India.

title: NICDC Advances Industrial Development in Bihar with Launch of Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited
subtitle:
12 MoUs signed for approximately 300 acres with proposed investments of ₹4,200 crore at IMC Gaya

Curtain raiser of Bihar Business Connect 2027 attended by approximately 250 delegates, including Ambassadors and senior representatives of the Embassies of Japan, Thailand and Laos
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) marked a significant milestone in advancing industrial development in Bihar with the formal launch of Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited (BIMCGL) by the Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary, at Bodh Gaya today. The event also marked the inauguration of the curtain raiser of Bihar Business Connect 2027, highlighting the State's industrial potential and investment opportunities.
A key highlight of the event was the signing of 12 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with prospective investors for approximately 300 acres of industrial land at IMC Gaya. These MoUs represent proposed investments of around ₹4,200 crore and an estimated employment potential of 16,095 opportunities. The proposed investments span sectors including food processing, automobile components, medicinal products, pharmaceuticals and other manufacturing activities.
Earlier, the Government of Bihar had also executed MoUs with prospective investors across multiple sectors at IMC Gaya, covering approximately 2,586 acres of land, with a total proposed investment of ₹31,750 crore and an estimated employment potential of 52,050 opportunities.
The programme was attended by approximately 250 delegates, including the Ambassadors and senior representatives of the Embassies of Japan, Thailand and Laos, senior government officials, representatives of the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC), industry associations and prospective investors. Representatives of Bihar Foundation Chapters from 55 countries also participated virtually.
During the programme, the Chief Minister unveiled the BIMCGL logo and launched its official website and Integrated Land Allotment Portal, aimed at strengthening investor facilitation, improving transparency and streamlining industrial land allotment.
Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary reiterated the State Government's commitment to accelerating industrial development, attracting investments and generating employment through improved infrastructure and investor-friendly initiatives.  Deputy Chief Minister Shri Vijay Kumar Choudhary made special mention of NICDC's role in the planning and development of IMC Gaya.
Union Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, highlighted the Government's determination to strengthen industrialisation in Bihar with continued support from the Central Government, particularly for promoting manufacturing, MSMEs and employment generation.
The programme was also attended by Deputy Chief Minister Shri Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Speaker of Bihar Vidhan Sabha Shri Prem Kumar and Minister of Industries Ms. Shreyasi Singh, along with other senior dignitaries. The State Government reaffirmed its commitment to supporting industrial development and facilitating investments.
BIMCGL is the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) responsible for implementing the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at Gaya, being developed under the Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) as part of the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP). Spread across 1,670 acres in Dobhi block of Gaya district, the project was approved by the Government of India on 28 August 2024 at a total cost of ₹1,339 crore, including land cost. It is expected to attract investments of approximately ₹16,500 crore and generate employment opportunities for around 1.10 lakh people.
Incorporated on 6 January 2025, BIMCGL is a joint venture between the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) and the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), with equal equity participation. As the dedicated implementing agency, BIMCGL will expedite project execution through coordinated planning, infrastructure development, statutory clearances, utility connectivity and investor facilitation. The institutional framework will enable faster decision-making, effective monitoring and timely resolution of implementation-related issues.
Infrastructure development at IMC Gaya is progressing, with the State Government having taken possession of the entire project land. The Government of India released the first tranche of equity amounting to ₹132 crore in September 2025 against the transfer of 415 acres. Project Management & Construction Supervision Consultant and EPC contractor for trunk infrastructure works had already been onboarded. The physical construction has already commenced.
Construction of an exclusive helipad at IMC Gaya is also at an advanced stage. It will enhance accessibility for investors, business delegations and senior officials, facilitating project monitoring and investment promotion activities.
The industrial cluster is being developed with integrated infrastructure, including internal roads, water supply, sewerage and wastewater treatment facilities, power distribution, solid waste management and fire safety systems. Its strategic location near NH-22 and NH-19, with Gaya Airport approximately 39 kilometres away, provides connectivity to major industrial and commercial centres. NICDC's role in planning the above, including assessing industrial water requirements and ensuring year-round water availability through adequate water storage facilities to support sustainable industrial operations, was formally acknowledged during the launch.
IMC Gaya will focus on sectors including agro-based industries, textiles and readymade garments, furniture, handicrafts and handloom, and engineering and fabrication. The planned infrastructure will support large manufacturers and MSMEs, encourage local entrepreneurship and strengthen industrial value chains across the region.
The curtain raiser of Bihar Business Connect 2027 provided an opportunity to showcase Bihar's investment potential and engage with prospective investors, industry associations and international stakeholders. The launch of BIMCGL reinforces the partnership between the Government of India and the Government of Bihar in developing modern, investment-ready industrial infrastructure.
With a dedicated institutional framework, ongoing infrastructure development and sustained investor engagement, BIMCGL is poised to accelerate the development of IMC Gaya as a major manufacturing destination in eastern India, contributing to Bihar's industrial transformation and the national vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Holds Meetings with German Industry Leaders and Research Institutions in Berlin
subtitle: India–Germany Economic Cooperation in Focus During Shri Goyal’s Berlin Visit
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 11:40AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal concluded his two-day official visit to Germany with a series of engagements in Berlin on 23 October 2026, including meetings with senior German government officials, business leaders, research institutions and members of the Indian diaspora. The engagements focused on strengthening India–Germany cooperation in trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, research and emerging technologies.
Shri Piyush Goyal held a bilateral meeting with the Economic and Financial Policy Advisor and G7/G20 Sherpa at the German Federal Chancellery, Mr. Levin Holle. The discussions covered bilateral economic cooperation and opportunities to further strengthen economic and investment ties between India and Germany.
The Minister held individual meetings with CEO, Siemens Healthineers AG, Mr. Bernd Montag; Mr. Carsten Coesfeld, Member of the Executive Board of Bertelsmann and CEO, Bertelsmann Investments; and, CFO, Volkswagen AG and CEO, Škoda Auto, Mr. Holger Peters. The meetings explored opportunities to expand business partnerships, investment and industrial cooperation between the two countries.
Shri Goyal also participated in a roundtable with leaders of prominent German industrial research institutions to discuss cooperation in advanced industrial technologies and innovation. Separately, members of the accompanying Indian business delegation participated in sectoral roundtables with German industry representatives and sectoral associations to explore opportunities for bilateral business collaboration.
Shri Goyal also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Berlin and addressed the media.
As part of his engagements with the research and innovation ecosystem, Shri Goyal interacted with Indian science and technology researchers and students based in Germany. He also held a roundtable with heads of selected Fraunhofer Institutes, covering areas such as microelectronics, power electronics, logistics, smart manufacturing, industrial innovation and battery technologies. The discussions explored avenues for strengthening research collaboration and industry–academia partnerships between India and Germany.
The engagements underscored the growing scope of the India–Germany Strategic Partnership, particularly in trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, science and technology, research and industrial cooperation.

title: Indigenous AIP system for Indian Navy’s diesel-electric submarines achieves key milestone with inauguration of Setting to Work Phase-2 Activity
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A significant milestone towards enhancing Indian Navy’s underwater capabilities has been achieved with the inauguration of ‘Setting to Work Phase (STW)-2’ activity of the Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system Energy Module developed indigenously by Naval Materials Research Laboratory, DRDO. The AIP system boosts the underwater endurance of the diesel-electric submarines by reducing its dependence on atmospheric oxygen.
The inauguration ceremony took place at Larsen and Toubro’s, AM Naik Heavy Engineering Complex in Hazira, Gujarat on October 24, 2026. Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh was the Chief Guest who graced the ceremony virtually. Chief of Materiel, Indian Navy Vice Admiral B Sivakumar and Director General (Naval Systems & Materials), DRDO Dr R Balamuralikrishnan attended the event at L&T Hazira, Gujarat.
Speaking on the occasion, the Chairman DRDO congratulated DRDO and the industry partners and appreciated the scientific perseverance & industrial cooperation in the indigenous AIP Program, which has culminated into productive reality on the shop floor. He also acknowledged the cooperation rendered by the Indian Navy to DRDO throughout the course of this programme, including testing and validating at every stage of the trials. He emphasised on working towards next phases of the program towards achieving Navy’s induction timelines for AIP system while maintaining the exacting safety culture that hydrogen and fuel cell systems require without compromise.
In the next phase, the AIP Energy Module will be energised for power production and tested rigorously as per Indian Navy’s protocols before handing over to Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited for integration on Kalvari-class Submarine in early 2027.

title: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh inaugurates World's first- of -its-kind 'Air Pollution Analysis' facility for Delhi NCR
subtitle:
'Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory ' (AATAL) also equipped to identify Real-Time Sources of Air Pollution

New facility to go beyond AQI numbers to reveal what is polluting Delhi’s air, where it is coming from and its potential health implications: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Integrated with AIRWISE to strengthen real-time source apportionment, air-quality forecasting and scientific decision-making, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Facility to support CAQM and pollution-control agencies in targeting interventions and assessing their effectiveness: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh says coordinated action across government departments is essential for evidence-based air pollution management
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today inaugurated the
world's first- of -its-kind 'Air Pollution Analysis' facility for Delhi NCR. Known as 'Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory ' (AATAL), it is also equipped to identify real-time sources of air pollution.
Describing it as a first-of-its-kind integrated facility in the world, the Minister said Delhi-NCR had been chosen in view of the serious public concern over air pollution. He said the facility would take air-quality assessment beyond simply reporting pollution levels to identifying the composition of pollutants, their sources, their relative contributions and their potential health implications, while providing real-time information and advance forecasts to support timely action.
The inauguration took place at IITM’s Delhi Branch in the presence of Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. A. Suryachandra Rao, Director, IITM and DG IMD Dr Mahapatra. The facility has been established under 'Mission Mausam' announced by PM Sh Narendra Modi to strengthen scientific understanding of atmospheric pollution and provide actionable evidence for air-quality management in Delhi-NCR. The laboratory brings together advanced atmospheric measurement instruments, detailed chemical analysis, pollution-source identification and decision-support capabilities within an integrated framework.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India had made substantial progress over the past 10–12 years in air-quality forecasting and analysis. He said the new facility represented a significant step forward because it would help establish not only how much pollution is present in the atmosphere, but also what it consists of and where it originates.
“Earlier, the discussion would largely revolve around whether the pollution level was 100 or 200. This facility will help us understand the composition of pollution as well as the contribution of different sources. This is important for addressing the concerns of the people of Delhi and ensuring that action is based on scientific evidence,” the Minister said.
AATAL will help scientists distinguish between different sources of air pollution, including vehicular emissions, industrial activity, biomass and crop-residue burning, construction and road dust, and pollutants transported from surrounding regions. By estimating the relative contribution of these sources, the facility will help authorities understand which activities are driving poor air quality at a particular time and where interventions may be most effective.
Explaining the significance of real-time source apportionment, Dr. Jitendra Singh cited an instance, while talking to the reporters, the screen showed that at that precise moment, transport was contributing approximately 25 per cent of Delhi air pollution, with the overall pollution level recorded at around 180. He said such information could help move the response to air pollution from general assessments to more targeted interventions based on the actual sources contributing to the problem.
The laboratory is equipped with advanced instruments for analysing the chemical composition of atmospheric gases and aerosols, including fine particulate matter (PM2.5), metals, toxic elements and other components. Its capabilities will help scientists investigate how pollutants interact and transform in the atmosphere and how different components contribute to the overall pollution burden.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the facility would provide information on the smaller constituents of air pollution, including metallic elements and other potentially harmful components. He explained that pollutants can differ in their health implications, making it important to understand not only their concentration but also their composition and potential toxicity.
The resulting scientific evidence can help health authorities better understand the potential risks associated with different types of particulate pollution. It can also support closer coordination between scientific institutions, health agencies and environmental authorities in assessing the implications of air pollution for public health.
The laboratory is integrated with IITM’s AIRWISE, Air Quality Warning and Integrated Decision Support System for Emissions, which combines air-quality forecasts, observations and source-apportionment information to support pollution management.
The project team explained that AIRWISE provides air-quality forecasts at a spatial resolution of 400 metres for the next 72 hours, enabling the system to assess how pollution may vary across different pockets of Delhi. It can also help identify the sources expected to contribute to deteriorating air quality in specific locations. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the integrated capability would provide real-time information as well as forecasts for the next four days, helping authorities prepare for changing pollution conditions.
Dr. Sachin Ghude, Project Director, MAQWS, said the integrated facility would strengthen air-quality management in Delhi-NCR by providing early warnings and detailed information on the sources contributing to pollution, including stubble burning, vehicular emissions, construction and road dust. He said the information would help the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and other implementing agencies identify the major sources of pollution, plan targeted interventions and assess their effectiveness.
He added that the associated air-quality forecasting system provides forecasts at a 400-metre resolution for the next 72 hours, enabling pollution levels and their likely sources to be assessed for individual pockets of Delhi. Describing the forecasting capability as a major technological advance, Dr. Ghude said India had developed a high-resolution system comparable with global forecasting systems, with the potential to extend similar capabilities to other cities.
Emphasising the importance of coordination among government agencies, Dr. Jitendra Singh said air pollution could not be addressed by a single department working in isolation. He described the initiative as an example of the whole-of-government approach advocated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, bringing together scientific institutions, environmental authorities, pollution-control agencies and disaster-management stakeholders.
The Minister said coordinated engagement among the Ministry of Earth Sciences, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, pollution-control authorities and disaster-management agencies would be important for translating scientific information into effective action.
For the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and other implementing agencies, the facility will provide measurement-based evidence to identify the sources responsible for deteriorating air quality, prioritise sectors and locations for intervention, and support coordinated measures across Delhi-NCR. When combined with AIRWISE forecasts, this information can strengthen decisions relating to preventive measures and responses under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).
The inauguration of AATAL marks an important step towards connecting advanced atmospheric science with public policy and on-ground action. By bringing real-time measurements, chemical characterisation, source apportionment and forecasting together, the facility will help authorities move towards a more precise understanding of air pollution and a more coordinated response to the challenge facing Delhi-NCR.

title: Digital India BHASHINI Division Showcases Multilingual AI Solutions for Accessible Research at ETD-2026, IIT Delhi
subtitle: BHASHINI explores collaboration with higher education institutions and research repositories to expand access to theses, dissertations and scholarly content across Indian languages
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 8:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
, Government of India, participated in the 29th International Symposium on Electronic Theses and Dissertations (ETD-2026), held at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi from 23 to 25 October 2026. Ms.
Baishali Chakraborty, speaking on behalf of DIBD
, conducted a session on BHASHINI’s multilingual artificial intelligence capabilities and their potential to make scholarly knowledge more accessible across languages.
Titled
“Workshop on AI BHASHINI: Bridging Divides and Increasing Productivity,”
the session highlighted how BHASHINI’s
Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)
can support higher education institutions, libraries and research repositories in addressing language barriers and expanding access to academic content.
During the session, Ms. Chakraborty
demonstrated
how
voice-first multilingual AI, speech-to-text, translation, optical character recognition (OCR) and document translation
can support multilingual access in academic and research settings. A live demonstration of
Shrutlekh
showcased real-time speech transcription with simultaneous translation, illustrating its potential applications in lecture halls, research seminars, conferences and academic discussions.
The session also highlighted BHASHINI’s broader multilingual AI ecosystem, which brings together language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications to support a range of language technology use cases. BHASHINI has recorded
over 10 billion cumulative AI inferences
and supports
36 Indian languages for text, 23 Indian languages for voice and 35 international languages
. Its website translation plugin enables multilingual access across
more than 800 government websites
.
A key focus of the session was the potential to extend
AI-powered translation to electronic theses and dissertations (ETDs)
, including lengthy and specialised academic documents.
BHASHINI Pragati
, a document translation workbench developed for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), was presented as an example of structured document translation and review. The workbench supports the processing of large documents, including those spanning
100 to 500 pages
, with quality checks and data security considerations.
The discussion explored how similar workflows could be adapted for research repositories such as
Shodhganga, maintained by INFLIBNET
, as well as universities and other higher education institutions. Such solutions could help make theses, dissertations, research reports and other scholarly material available across Indian languages while preserving document structure, specialised terminology and meaning.
Speaking on the occasion, Harshad Sharma, Senior Manager (Finance), Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), said,
“
Making research and scholarly knowledge accessible across Indian languages is an important step towards a more inclusive knowledge ecosystem. BHASHINI’s multilingual AI capabilities, including document translation and speech technologies, can help universities, libraries and research repositories reach wider audiences. Engagement with academic institutions will be key to understanding their requirements and developing reliable solutions for multilingual access to theses, dissertations and other research content.”
During the interaction, participants raised questions about translating PDF documents on the fly and the reliability of AI translation for specialised academic and scientific content. Ms. Chakraborty discussed the importance of combining domain-specific machine translation with human review and quality assurance. The discussion also explored opportunities to work with research organisations to understand their requirements and develop customised solutions suited to their repositories and academic domains.
The session further covered BHASHINI’s capabilities in
OCR for extracting text from scanned documents and images, terminology management through SHABD UDYAN, and transliteration
to help preserve technical terms, names and expressions across scripts. These capabilities can support workflows that improve the accessibility and discoverability of research content while accounting for the linguistic and formatting requirements of academic documents.
Beyond translation, the session highlighted
BhashaDaan
, BHASHINI’s citizen-contribution initiative, which helps build and enrich language resources through speech and text contributions, audio transcription, and text extraction from images and documents.
Granthika
was also presented as a tool for digitising and preserving books, manuscripts, literary works, folk tales and oral histories, contributing to the development of digital resources for India’s multilingual knowledge ecosystem.
BHASHINI invited higher education institutions, research repositories, libraries and academic organisations to explore collaboration in identifying priority use cases, developing domain-specific language resources and adapting translation workflows to their needs. Such engagement can help address repository-specific requirements, strengthen translation quality through human validation and expand multilingual access to India’s scholarly output.
BHASHINI’s participation at ETD-2026 reflects its broader objective of advancing language technology as a public digital resource. Engagement with academic institutions and research repositories offers an opportunity to extend multilingual AI capabilities to scholarly communication, helping research and knowledge reach audiences across linguistic boundaries.
About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is advancing India’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure to enable multilingual access to digital services. BHASHINI brings together language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications to support government departments, developers, researchers and other stakeholders in building multilingual AI solutions. It powers more than 800 government websites, has enabled over 10 billion cumulative AI inferences and supports 36 Indian languages for text, 23 Indian languages for voice and 35 international languages, advancing language technology across India’s digital ecosystem.

title: Agricultural Biological Resources generate around ₹1.04 Crore in ABS Benefits for Biodiversity Initiatives across India
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:

content:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed around Rs. 1.04 crore of Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) amount among 27 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), two Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs). This demonstrates how benefits arising from the utilisation of agricultural biological resources can be channelled towards biodiversity conservation and sustainable use.
The amount represents benefit-sharing contributions received from Crystal Crop Protection Limited, Savannah Seeds Pvt. Ltd. and Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. for access to agricultural biological resources for research and commercial purposes. The contributions relate to the utilisation of pearl millet (
Pennisetum glaucum
), jowar (
Sorghum bicolor
), maize (
Zea mays
), rice (
Oryza sativa
L.) and bottle gourd (
Lagenaria siceraria
). These crops are important components of India’s agricultural biodiversity, supporting food security, farming livelihoods and agricultural innovation.
NBA has adopted an area-based approach to distribute the benefit-sharing component, where biological resources are procured through markets, traders or intermediaries and individual benefit claimers cannot be identified. Allocations are determined proportionately, taking into account the geographical distribution and cultivation area of the relevant crops, based on agricultural statistics published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare through its Unified Portal for Agricultural Statistics.
The disbursal of around Rs. 1.04 crore covers allocations to SBBs and UTBCs. The state-wise distribution includes allocations for the top 10 States and the remaining States collectively, based on the applicable area-based methodology.

These contributions can support the conservation and sustainable use of agricultural biological resources, including traditional crop varieties and genetic diversity, while strengthening biodiversity-related initiatives at the State and Union Territory levels.
Till date, the NBA has released over Rs. 204 crore ($21.48 mn) in ABS benefits, supporting biodiversity conservation and benefit sharing across the country. India’s ABS framework contributes to the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Nagoya Protocol and supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which calls for effective measures to ensure the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources, digital sequence information and associated traditional knowledge.
India’s experience in implementing ABS will be highlighted at the CBD COP 17 side event ‘From Policy to Practice: Advancing India’s Biodiversity Commitments through Innovation, Finance, and ABS’, scheduled on 28th October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia. The event will showcase India’s efforts to translate biodiversity commitments into action through policy implementation, innovation, financing and benefit sharing.
Funds allocated to SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and for activities relating to biodiversity conservation and sustainable use, documentation, research, capacity building and strengthening local biodiversity governance, as applicable. India’s ABS framework is governed by the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024, and the Access and Benefit-Sharing Regulations, 2025. Section 21 of the Act provides for the determination of fair and equitable benefit sharing arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The present release of money demonstrates the practical application of this framework in agricultural supply chains, linking research and commercial utilisation with support for biodiversity-related initiatives.

title: CAQM reviews Paddy Stubble Management measures in Amritsar and Tarn Taran
subtitle: Directs Field Officers to ensure Timely Availability and Maximizing Facilities for Utilisation of Paddy Stubble
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A high-level team led by Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), today held a review meeting with the Deputy Commissioners and other concerned officers of Amritsar and Tarn Taran districts of Punjab. The meeting reviewed the measures being undertaken for comprehensive management of paddy stubble. It also focused on further containing and eliminating incidents of paddy stubble burning.
The team reviewed the
in-situ
and
ex-situ
utilisation of paddy stubble management, facilities and infrastructure for stubble management in the two Districts. The action taken by two District in light of the increased number of fire incidents was also reviewed. The team expressed concern at the increased number of fire incidents, and the concerned officers were directed to ensure all the efforts to arrest the numbers henceforth.
The Commission emphasized on ensuring maximum utilisation of paddy stubble as a fuel in thermal power plants, brick kilns and industries where such fuel usage is feasible. The Commission further directed that sector-wise Nodal Officers must be given responsibility for ensuring actual utilisation of paddy stubble by the respective sectors/ industries and for regularly monitoring and reporting compliance.
Emphasising the importance of timely field-level intervention, the Commission directed the officers to undertake regular visits to villages and farmers and not merely inform them about the availability of stubble management facilities but also ensure that the required machinery and facilities reach the farmers in a timely manner. The District Administrations were asked to strengthen coordination between farmers, Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs), machinery providers and other stakeholders so that farmers are able to access residue management solutions without delay.
As Tarn Taran District continues to report amongst the highest number of paddy stubble burning incidents, the Deputy Commissioner was directed to accord topmost priority to the issue and intensify field-level measures for prevention and management of such incidents. The Commission also warned that any laxity or failure in taking effective measures would invite strict action and accountability.
During the visit, the high-level team also inspected facilities in Amritsar where paddy stubble is being utilised as a source of fuel. The team visited the industrial boiler at an industrial complex in Amritsar, where paddy stubble pellets are being used as fuel in the industrial boiler. The visit provided an opportunity to assess the practical utilisation of processed paddy residue and the potential for scaling up such productive end-use models.
The Commission reiterated that paddy stubble management needs to be approached as a comprehensive residue-management and resource-utilisation exercise from the farmer facilitation standpoint. It was stressed that concerted efforts by District Administrations must be made by all concerned stakeholders to ensure that available
in-situ
and
ex-situ
solutions are effectively deployed, residue is channelized for productive use and incidents of paddy stubble burning are brought to an end.

title: 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition concludes in Bhubaneswar with participation of around 1,500 delegates and experts
subtitle:
Urban Mobility must be integrated with Urban Planning from the outset: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal

Union Minister calls for Integration, Inclusiveness and Intelligence as the three pillars of future urban mobility

Over ₹59,000 crore worth of nine Metro projects approved since December 2025; 1,100 electric buses operational in 28 cities: Shri Manohar Lal

Union Minister presents Awards for Excellence and Best Practices in Urban Transport; 28 exhibitors showcase innovations and mobility solutions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 concluded in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, today, with Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, addressing the valedictory session and presenting awards for excellence and best practices in urban transport. The two-day Conference, held on 23–24 October 2026, was organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) through the Institute of Urban Transport (India), with the support of the Government of Odisha.
The valedictory session was attended by Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Government of Odisha; Smt. Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha; and other senior officials, policymakers, urban transport experts and delegates from India and abroad.
Addressing the valedictory session, Shri Manohar Lal
emphasised that urban mobility must be integrated with urban planning from the very beginning. He said that better transport infrastructure is no longer merely an outcome of development but has become a foundation for economic growth and urban development. He highlighted the importance of planning cities around the mobility needs of citizens, ensuring easy access to workplaces, schools, hospitals and other essential services.
The Minister stated that India’s future urban mobility systems must be guided by the three principles of
Integration, Inclusiveness and Intelligence (3-I)
. He explained that Integration means seamless connectivity between metro, bus, rail and other transport services, with strong first- and last-mile connectivity. Inclusiveness calls for safe, accessible and convenient transport for women, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and all sections of society. Intelligence involves the use of Artificial Intelligence and real-time data to improve traffic management, passenger safety and efficiency of public transport.
Highlighting progress in urban transport infrastructure, Shri Manohar Lal informed that since December 2025, the Government of India has approved nine Metro projects covering approximately 174 kilometres at a cost of over ₹59,000 crore. During the same period, an additional 102 kilometres of Metro network has become operational. He further stated that India’s operational Metro network has expanded to 1,185 kilometres across 26 cities.
The Minister also highlighted progress under the PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme. He informed that 1,100 electric buses have commenced operations in 28 cities, carrying an average of around 2.5 lakh passengers daily. Referring to the Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Policy 2026 approved for Delhi in April 2026, he said that the policy will promote planned development and affordable housing across approximately 207 square kilometres along Metro, RRTS and railway corridors.
Referring to the deliberations during the Conference, the Minister said that 14 sessions were organised over two days, with participation from around 1,500 delegates and experts from India and abroad. He noted that 28 exhibitors showcased innovations and solutions in urban transport. He highlighted that the discussions had placed particular emphasis on integrating mobility into city planning and using data from telecom networks, mobile applications and digital platforms for evidence-based planning of Metro, bus and other transport services.
Shri Manohar Lal expressed satisfaction that the Conference had also focused on walking, cycling, people-centric streets and the mobility needs of women, senior citizens and persons with disabilities. Congratulating the States, cities and organisations recognised for excellence in urban transport, he urged all stakeholders to translate the suggestions emerging from the Conference into concrete action plans that deliver tangible benefits to citizens.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra
, Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Government of Odisha, said that the true success of a conference lies not merely in the ideas discussed but in translating them into meaningful action on the ground. He stated that the 19th Urban Mobility India Conference had provided a valuable platform for policymakers, urban experts, industry partners and other stakeholders to exchange experiences, innovative ideas and best practices. He emphasised that the learnings from the Conference must be converted into practical solutions suited to the needs of cities, with a focus on making urban spaces safer, more accessible, inclusive and liveable.
Additional Chief Secretary, Housing and Urban
Development, Govt. Of Odisha in her remarks said “Odisha is proud to have hosted the 19th Urban Mobility India Conference & Exhibition and the National Urban Conclave 2026. The discussions and deliberations over the past few days have been truly enriching and engaging, bringing together valuable ideas and perspectives on sustainable urban development and people-centric mobility. As hosts, we endeavoured to uphold the spirit of Atithi Devo Bhava, ensuring that every delegate felt welcomed and valued in Odisha. We hope the insights and collaborations emerging from this platform will translate into meaningful action towards building inclusive, accessible and sustainable cities for the future.”
Awards for Excellence and Best Practices in Urban Transport
During the valedictory session, Shri Manohar Lal, along with Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, presented awards recognising excellence and best practices in urban transport. The awards acknowledged innovative initiatives undertaken by cities, States and transport organisations to improve public transport, promote sustainable mobility and strengthen urban transport systems.
The following organisations were recognised across different categories:
City with the Best Green Transport Initiative:
Bhubaneswar – Comprehensive Region Urban Transport (CRUT).
City with the Best Non-Motorized Transport System:
Chennai – Greater Chennai Corporation.
Excellence in Innovation & Smart Mobility Solutions:
Delhi – Delhi Transport Corporation and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.

Delhi – Delhi Transport Corporation.
Metro Station with Best Multi-modal Integration:
Kochi – Kochi Metro Rail Ltd.
Metro Rail with the Best Passenger Services and Satisfaction:
Chennai Metro Rail Ltd. and National Capital Region Transport Corporation (Delhi/Uttar Pradesh).

Delhi – Delhi Transport Corporation.

Technical Sessions and Deliberations
The second day of the Conference featured technical sessions, round table discussions and a plenary session covering various aspects of sustainable and integrated urban mobility.
The
Technical Session on ‘Land Use and Transport Beyond City Limits – TOD, Urban Form and Peri-Urban Corridors’
focused on integrating land-use and transport planning beyond traditional city boundaries. Discussions covered Transit-Oriented Development, compact urban growth, mixed-use development along mass transit corridors and the need for seamless connectivity between suburban areas and major transport networks. The session also examined governance challenges, affordable housing linkages and financing mechanisms for developing transit-oriented peri-urban corridors.
The
Round Table on ‘People-Centric Streets – Safe, Walkable, Cyclable’
discussed the importance of designing urban streets that prioritise pedestrians, cyclists and public safety. Deliberations covered continuous footpaths, protected cycling networks, safe crossings, traffic-calming measures and institutional mechanisms for developing accessible and people-friendly streets.
The
Round Table on ‘Behaviour Change and Public Communication – Enhancing Modal Shift through Public Outreach’
examined strategies to encourage citizens to shift from private vehicles to sustainable modes of transport. Discussions focused on targeted communication campaigns, community participation, incentives, digital applications and behavioural change initiatives to increase the use of public transport.
The
Round Table on ‘Intelligence Driven Safe and Secure Mobility’
focused on the application of Artificial Intelligence, real-time data, connected infrastructure and emerging digital technologies in improving urban transport safety and efficiency. The discussions explored the potential of intelligent traffic management systems, connected vehicles and technology-enabled solutions for safer and more reliable mobility.
The
Plenary Session on ‘Rail-Led Integrated Urban Development’
discussed the role of Metro and other mass rapid transit systems in shaping sustainable and liveable cities. Deliberations highlighted the need for economically viable rail-based transport systems, seamless multimodal integration and stronger first- and last-mile connectivity. The session also examined how mass transit infrastructure can support integrated urban growth and future-ready mobility networks.
Conference Highlights
The 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition was held under the theme
‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’
. The Conference brought together policymakers, senior officials from Central and State Governments, international experts, transport professionals, researchers and industry representatives to deliberate on emerging challenges and opportunities in urban mobility.
An exhibition featuring 28 exhibitors from the Government of Odisha, Metro Rail Companies, public sector organisations and private sector entities showcased emerging technologies, innovations and best practices in urban transport.
The Conference also provided a platform for research scholars and PhD students through a Research Symposium, with 46 selected research papers comprising 20 oral presentations and 26 poster presentations.
The Conference concluded with a renewed emphasis on integrated planning, evidence-based decision-making, technological innovation and inclusive public transport systems to improve accessibility and quality of life in Indian cities.

title: National Urban Conclave 2026 inaugurated in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
subtitle:
Three things must be looked at: systems that plan and govern our cities, the solutions we apply on the ground, and the way services are finally delivered to citizens :Shri Tokhan Sahu,MoS MoHUA

Odisha is moving towards a new era of planned urbanisation, modern infrastructure and sustainable mobility, guided by the vision of Samruddha Odisha and Viksit Bharat 2047 : Shri Mohan Charan Majhi

Day-one deliberations focused on seven thematic areas
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The second edition of the National Urban Conclave was inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Union Minister of State, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The Conclave, being held on 24-25 October 2026, is organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and  supported by State Government of Odisha. National Institute of Urban Affairs is  the knowledge partner with Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited, National Buildings Construction Corporation Limited, as the principal sponsors.
Organised under the theme ‘Urban Rising - Rethinking Urban Systems, Solutions and Delivery’, it brings together over 1,200 participants at the venue  including urban development Ministers, Mayors,  and representatives from urban local bodies (ULB), urban development authorities, academia, industry, civil society, and the wider urban development ecosystem.
The conclave focuses on
reimagining systems, institutions, and implementation mechanisms that shape how cities function.
Inauguration of the Conclave
Lighting the ceremonial lamp during the inaugural session, Shri Tokhan Sahu, the Hon’ble Union Minister of State, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, emphasised India’s ongoing urban transformation, wherein urban population had grown from approximately 377 million in 2011 to around 500 million, and is expected to reach 600 million by 2036. By the centenary of India’s independence, nearly one in every two Indians would live in a city. He noted that national programmes, including PMAY, AMRUT, Swachh Bharat Mission, PM SVANidhi, DAY-NULM and the Smart Cities Mission, had laid a strong foundation for the next phase of urban development.
Gracing the occasion, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi,
Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha shared the state’s ambition to become a key growth engine in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047. “Odisha is moving towards a new era of planned urbanisation, modern infrastructure and sustainable mobility, guided by the vision of Samruddha Odisha and Viksit Bharat 2047. As we work towards building a $500 billion economy by 2036, our focus is on creating inclusive, technology-enabled and people-centric cities. The expansion of Ama Bus services, the introduction of electric buses and the development of the Bhubaneswar-Kataka-Puri-Paradip Economic Region reflect our commitment to cleaner mobility, better urban infrastructure and improved quality of life for our citizens. We are building cities that are not only engines of economic growth but also safer, more accessible and more liveable for everyone”, he said.
Speaking on the occasion Smt. Anu Garg,
Chief Secretary of Odisha stated “Urban mobility is about much more than roads, buses and infrastructure; it is about people, their dignity and their everyday experiences. Urban development must begin with the basic needs of citizens—access to safe drinking water, efficient public transport, clean surroundings and well-planned public spaces. Odisha’s expansion of the Drink from Tap initiative to 11 cities, along with piped drinking water coverage across 114 urban areas, reflects our commitment to reliable and citizen-centric urban services. As our cities grow, we must ensure that infrastructure and public services keep pace with urbanisation, while recognising the frontline workers who play a vital role in keeping our cities moving. Through coordinated planning, institutional strengthening and effective implementation, we must translate urban reforms into tangible improvements in the everyday lives of our citizens.”
Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban
Development, highlighted the opportunity to rethink urban systems, co-create innovative solutions, and strengthen delivery mechanisms to make cities more liveable, inclusive, resilient, and future-ready. He highlighted the role of flagship initiatives, including Swachh Bharat Mission, AMRUT, Housing for All, metro rail, PM-eBus Sewa and PM SVANidhi, in improving service delivery, encouraging citizen participation and strengthening urban resilience. He also outlined recent initiatives and reforms, including the Urban Challenge Fund of ₹1 lakh crore, the ₹5,000 crore Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme, the ₹10,000 crore Urbanisation Premium Grant recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission, and reforms under the SASCI Scheme.
Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog,
in his keynote address stated the importance of institutionalising dialogue and sustaining engagement with state governments to advance India’s urban development agenda. He noted that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 emerged through extensive participation and consultation, highlighting cities' role in driving societal and economic development. With nearly 50 per cent of India’s population expected to be urban by 2047, contributing around 75 per cent of GDP, he stressed the need for well-planned and coordinated urbanisation, supported by three pillars: investment, institutional response and capacity building.
Smt Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha, delivered the vote of thanks, expressing appreciation for the opportunity to host the National Urban Conclave and showcase Odisha’s initiatives and experiences in urban development. She noted that the Conclave gave urban practitioners and stakeholders an opportunity to gain insights and learn from the state’s efforts. She extended her gratitude to the Hon’ble Minister of State, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, senior officials, state commissioners, and all those who contributed to the organisation of the conclave.
Launches and Releases
The inaugural programme launched several initiatives and publications
Urban Invest Window (UiWIN) Journal
HUDCO's Urban Invest Window (UiWIN), supports states and ULBs through project development, capacity building and the preparation of investment-ready projects. Strong project preparation and innovative financing are essential for converting urban aspirations into implementable projects that create tangible benefits for citizens.
Samarthya Platform for CPHEEO
Integrated portal for knowledge management and capacity building in solid waste / used water/water sector.
ANKUR Handbook
The ANKUR Handbook: 2025–26 Key Achievements and 2026–27 Reform Priorities, presents the progress and outcomes of Atal Network for Knowledge, Urbanisation and Reform (ANKUR). The handbook highlights work across urban planning, municipal finance, institutional capacity building and digital governance through SUJOG.
Odisha Town Planning Handbooks
Developed by the Directorate of Town Planning, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha, in collaboration with NIUA, the handbooks aim to simplify urban planning procedures and regulations, and offer citizens guidance on building plan and layout plan approvals.
Framework on Government and Privately Owned Public Spaces for Odisha
The proposed Government-Owned Public Spaces (GOPS) and Privately-Owned Public Spaces (POPS) Policy seeks to expand access to inclusive, accessible and well-maintained public spaces. GOPS focuses on activating underutilised government and institutional land, while POPS integrates publicly accessible plazas, landscaped areas and community spaces into private developments through planning regulations and incentives.
E-Book: Mera Ghar Mera Abhimaan
A compendium celebrating the voices and experiences of beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Urban. (PMAY-U)
E-Launch of PMAY-U 2.0 Mobile Application
The application is an updated version of the existing mobile application.
Standard Operating Procedure for PMAY-U Awards 2027
The SOP will establish the parameters and framework against which States' performance will be assessed, further encouraging and strengthening implementation of urban housing interventions.
Advisory on C & D Waste Management
This advisory for ULBs outlines how to implement the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules 2025, which supersede the 2016 rules with a circular economy approach built on Extended Producer Responsibility, mandatory waste management and utilisation plans, recycling targets, and an online compliance portal.
Outcome Report on ‘Adequate Housing for All’
The Outcome Report collates the deliberations and recommendations of the technical sessions held on World Habitat Day, 2026, which examined how the potential of rental housing can be unlocked, what regulatory interventions can help bridge the gap between housing demand and supply, and how local and indigenous technologies can help scale up resilient, affordable housing.
The ‘Guidance Document on Compliance of Bulk Waste Generators’ was also launched.
Technical Deliberations
The first day of the Conclave featured seven thematic deliberations.
The session on ‘Right to Walk’ addressed an everyday concern in our cities: how to make streets safer and more accessible through continuous footpaths, safe school zones, better pedestrian crossings and improved last-mile connectivity.
Under ‘Water, Waste and Resource Efficiency’, the emphasis was on moving beyond infrastructure creation to improving service efficiency, reducing water losses, promoting treated-water reuse and recovering value from waste.
The session on ‘Affordable Housing’ brought attention to the growing need for rental accommodation, simpler regulatory approvals, better access to land and finance, and wider adoption of affordable, climate-resilient construction technologies.
Through ‘Integrated Urban Development and Infrastructure Delivery’, the session examined how better coordination between agencies, integrated utility planning and GIS-based systems can reduce duplication and improve the planning and execution of urban infrastructure.
A key question under the session on ‘New Paradigms for Urban Service Delivery’ was how municipalities can deliver better services through clearer institutional responsibilities, stronger finances, procurement reforms, technical capacity and partnerships with the private sector.
The session on ‘Model Building Bye-Laws’ focussed on how the existing regulatory framework can be revised to simplify building approvals, strengthen safety and accessibility, and respond to climate resilience and emerging construction technologies.
Finally, ‘Model Municipal Law’ examined the legislative reforms needed to strengthen municipal autonomy, clarify the powers of elected representatives and executive authorities, and improve institutional capacity and accountability in urban governance.

date:

content:
The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh, will hold a
Two-Day State-Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection
on
26th and 27th October 2026
at
Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
. This event is being organised as part of the nationwide
“Shram Samvad”
initiative focusing on district-level capacity building and awareness on labour reforms.
The Shram Samvad campaign, launched nationwide on September 28, 2026, is a 90-day outreach initiative through which the Ministry is undertaking district-level engagement across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories, with a special focus on industrial clusters. The initiative seeks to provide employers and other stakeholders with greater clarity on the provisions, applicability, and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes, thereby facilitating effective ground-level implementation.
Day 1 of the Programme will see deliberations centred around 'Labour Reforms', with the keynote address being delivered by the Secretary (Labour & Employment). Key sessions in the first half of the day will throw light on international labour mobility, social protection measures for Unorganised and Gig/Platform Workers, and initiatives for Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW).
The Minister for Labour and Employment, Government of Uttar Pradesh, will address one of the key sessions in the second half of the day, with following sessions bringing in insights from the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) and Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). Discussions will also underline the significance of leveraging technology for workers’ welfare through platforms like e-Shram, Shram Suvidha Portal, SAMADHAN and Labour Stack, along with best practices and rollout strategies by the state government.
Day 2 will focus on 'Implementation of Labour Codes & Way Forward', beginning with technical sessions chaired by senior officials from the Ministry. Deliberations in the first half of the day will feature an overview and detailed breakdown of statutory compliances under all four Labour Codes, i.e., Code on Wages (2019), Industrial Relations Code (2020), Code on Social Security (2020), and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (2020). This will be followed by dedicated presentations on flagship schemes, including the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana. Devendranagar-Churhat New Passenger Train Service Flagged Off; Will Serve as a Lifeline for Local Students, Patients and Daily Commuters

Mineral-Rich Vindhya Region Connected with Major Industrial and Transport Centres Across the Country, Boosting the Rural Economy of the Region

content:
A historic milestone was achieved today in the expansion of rail connectivity in the Vindhya region of Madhya Pradesh. In the presence of Hon’ble Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav, Satna-Devendranagar and Rewa-Churhat rail sections were inaugurated. The programme held at Churhat Railway Station was attended by Deputy Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Shri Rajendra Shukla, Member of Parliament from Rewa Shri Janardan Mishra, Member of Parliament from Sidhi Shri Rajesh Mishra, along with other public representatives and dignitaries. The programme held at Nagod Railway Station was attended by Minister of State in the Government of Madhya Pradesh Smt. Pratima Bagri, Member of Parliament from Satna Shri Ganesh Singh, Member of Parliament from Khajuraho Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma, along with other public representatives and dignitaries.

Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said that improved rail connectivity is establishing a new lifeline for the Vindhya and Bundelkhand regions. He said that the project would fulfil a long-standing demand and improve access to education, employment and healthcare services for the people of the region.
Shri Vaishnaw referred to the expansion of railway connectivity across the country and highlighted the work undertaken in Srinagar, Mizoram and at the Pamban Bridge. He also mentioned the recent achievement of connecting Raoghat in Chhattisgarh and Tanda Road in Madhya Pradesh to the railway network.
The commencement of rail operations on the Devendranagar-Satna and Rewa-Churhat rail sections under the Lalitpur-Singrauli Railway Project will further strengthen connectivity in the Vindhya and Bundelkhand regions. He said that improved rail connectivity would accelerate industrial development in Madhya Pradesh and expand economic activities.
The Railway Minister stated that railway projects worth approximately ₹1 lakh crore are underway in Madhya Pradesh. These include new railway lines, doubling, construction of third and fourth railway lines, and gauge conversion projects. Work is being undertaken on railway sections such as Lalitpur-Singrauli, Satna-Rewa, Katni-Singrauli, Jabalpur-Gondia, Bina-Bhopal-Itarsi, Itarsi-Nagpur, Ratlam-Khandwa, Indore-Budni, Indore-Dahod and Indore-Manmad.
He said that the completion of these projects would pave the way for the introduction of new train services in the state. In the coming years, more than 100 long-distance trains and 50 to 60 short-distance train services, such as MEMU and Intercity trains, could be introduced.
Regarding station redevelopment, Shri Vaishnaw stated that Khajuraho station is being developed with architecture reflecting the culture and heritage of Madhya Pradesh. In addition, redevelopment work is being undertaken at several stations, including Ashoknagar, Balaghat, Beohari, Nainpur, Narmadapuram, Chhatarpur, Orchha, Shivpuri, Harpalpur, Chhindwara and Seoni. He also mentioned that approximately 80 railway stations in the state have been included under the redevelopment programme.
Emphasising the environmental commitments associated with the railway project, the Railway Minister referred to the felling of trees in the Anna region. He stated that a plan had been made to plant more saplings than the number of trees felled. He directed the General Manager, Divisional Railway Manager and District Magistrate to visit the site and inspect the plantation, ensure the survival of the planted saplings and plant new saplings wherever required.
Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav said during the programme that the new rail connectivity marked a fresh beginning for the Bundelkhand and Vindhya regions, bringing railway services to areas that had remained unconnected by rail. He described the occasion as a Diwali gift for the people of the region.
Dr. Yadav said that the 541-km-long Lalitpur-Singrauli Railway Project would strengthen connectivity between Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, benefiting the regions of Lalitpur, Chhatarpur, Panna, Satna, Rewa, Sidhi and Singrauli.
The Chief Minister said that improved rail connectivity would provide farmers access to larger markets, facilitate freight transportation for industries, create opportunities for young people and students, improve access to healthcare services and promote tourism. He said that connectivity would boost economic activities in the mineral-rich Bundelkhand region, particularly benefiting the diamond trade in Panna. He also appreciated the railway projects being undertaken in Madhya Pradesh, including the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga-Khandwa railway line.
Rewa-Churhat Railway Line to Benefit Sidhi District
The approximately 65-km-long new railway line from Rewa to Churhat has been constructed at a cost of approximately ₹1,070 crore. The project was completed with the completion of the final approximately 22.5-km railway line section between Rampur Naikin and Churhat. With rail connectivity extending to Churhat, residents of Sidhi district have gained an opportunity to connect with the national railway network.
This railway line is not merely a new mode of transportation for the region but also a means of creating new development opportunities. It will facilitate access for students to educational institutions, patients to better medical facilities, and young people and working professionals to employment and business opportunities. Considering the availability of limestone and other minerals in the region, along with the potential for the cement industry, rail connectivity is also expected to encourage industrial activities and freight transportation.
Satna-Devendranagar Railway Line to Boost Industrial and Rural Economy
The approximately 53-km-long new railway line from Satna to Devendranagar has been constructed at a cost of approximately ₹873 crore. The project was completed with the completion of the final 8-km railway line section between Phulwari and Devendranagar.
Satna and its surrounding areas have a significant presence of limestone, cement and other mineral-based industries. Improved rail connectivity will help facilitate the transportation of cement, clinker and other goods. This will improve the logistics arrangements of industries, reduce dependence on road-based freight transportation and enhance the prospects for the expansion of industrial activities in the future.
Rail connectivity will also provide farmers and rural traders in the Devendranagar, Nagod and Panna regions with better options for accessing larger markets. Railway connectivity will help agricultural produce, local products and handicrafts reach wider markets. In addition, new employment opportunities are likely to emerge in warehousing, transportation, trade and other allied activities.
New Passenger Train Service to Facilitate Students, Patients and Daily Commuters
With the commencement of the new Devendranagar-Churhat-Devendranagar passenger train service, passengers in the concerned areas will have improved rail connectivity through Satna and Rewa. This will provide a convenient travel option for students, working professionals, traders, patients, farmers and other daily commuters.
The new rail connectivity will also enhance the prospects of transporting local agricultural produce, stone crafts, handicrafts and other products to larger markets. This may provide a boost to local trade, transportation, food services and other small businesses.
Tourism to Receive a Boost, Local Employment Opportunities to Increase
The Vindhya and Bundelkhand regions are known for their natural beauty, historical heritage and numerous sites of cultural significance. Improved rail connectivity will help facilitate access to tourist destinations in Panna, Khajuraho, Rewa and the surrounding areas.
Major tourist attractions in the region include the White Tiger Safari, Mukundpur, Chachai and Bahuti waterfalls, Rewa Fort and Govindgarh. Improved rail connectivity is expected to make travel to these destinations more convenient and promote regional tourism. An increase in tourist movement may also benefit hotels, local transport services, guides, handicrafts and small businesses.
