title: 8th All India Conference of GRP Chiefs Concludes in New Delhi; Focus on Intelligence-Led Policing and Stronger Coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police
subtitle:
GRP Personnel Onboarded on RailMadad Platform for Improved Grievance Redressal, Timely Information-Sharing and Complaint Monitoring

Safer Railway Journeys During Diwali and Chhath: Emphasis on Crowd Management, Advance Planning and Efficient Passenger-Flow Management

From Drone-Assisted “Pink Patrol” to Project DISHA, Women-Led and Community-Based Safety Initiatives Deliberated at GRP Chiefs’ Conference
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 8th All India Conference of Government Railway Police (GRP) Chiefs, convened by the Railway Protection Force (RPF), concluded successfully in New Delhi on 23 October 2026. It provided a platform for discussing emerging security challenges, sharing best practices and strengthening coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police.
The high-level conference was presided over by Director General, RPF, Ms. Sonali Mishra, and attended by Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, Shri Satish Kumar, members of the Railway Board, and GRP chiefs from various States and Union Territories.
A key highlight was the onboarding of GRP personnel onto the RailMadad platform by the Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), aimed at improving passenger grievance redressal, timely information-sharing and complaint monitoring.
Detailed deliberations were held on various initiatives aimed at enhancing railway security and passenger safety.
South Central Railway’s “Pink Patrol: Eyes in the Sky, SHAKTI on the Ground” showcased a women-led model integrating drone-assisted surveillance with rapid-response teams under the SHAKTI framework.
Stone-pelting on trains was highlighted as a challenge, with emphasis on hotspot-based patrolling, enhanced surveillance, strict action against offenders, youth outreach and stronger RPF-GRP coordination. Community awareness and preventive engagement were recognised as important deterrents.
The conference also deliberated on crowd management during Diwali, Chhath and other festivals. Northern Railway’s Delhi Division highlighted coordinated efforts with Delhi Police, GRP and Delhi Metro authorities, supported by CCTV surveillance, public announcements, barricading, designated holding areas and dedicated control rooms. Emphasis was laid on advance planning, efficient passenger-flow management and coordinated deployment of security personnel to ensure safe and orderly passenger movement during peak periods.
Central Railway’s Pune Division highlighted Project DISHA (Dedicated Initiative for Safety, Harmony & Awareness), an initiative aimed at engaging children living near railway tracks through educational and recreational activities, safety awareness sessions and community-based interventions. Collaboration with NGOs, National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers and local communities fosters awareness about railway safety and responsible behaviour, while discouraging stone-pelting, theft, trespassing and other unsafe practices.
Deliberations also covered joint RPF-GRP training, sabotage prevention and prompt information-sharing on narcotics detection. Digital evidence handling, standardised procedures, intelligence-sharing, strengthened investigative capabilities and supporting infrastructure were emphasised.
Addressing the gathering, the Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, highlighted the importance of coordinated efforts, technological advancements, innovation and a shared commitment among railway authorities, RPF, GRP and State Police to effectively address the evolving security challenges on Indian Railways. He also emphasised the need to build passenger confidence, ensure courteous and professional policing, and leverage technology and innovation to enhance productivity and operational efficiency.
The conference concluded with closing remarks by DG/RPF, who emphasised the need for intelligence-led policing to strengthen railway security.

The 08 days
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 is underway at Guwahati, the State Capital of Assam. The Mela is 2nd of the Shilp Samagam Mela Series being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, during Financial Year 2026-27.
As part of bringing together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, the M
ela
showcases India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the
Mela will continue until October 28 Wednesday.
He said the Mela remains open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock.
The Official said the visitors are exploring the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.
He said the the visitors also witness and enjoy traditional musical and dance programmes presented by a galaxy of artists.
The Official said a total of
75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela
, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.
He said the event is providing participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach.
By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.
The Official said the Guwahati edition features a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India.
The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.
He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.
The Official further said a key focus of the Mela is the promotion of
BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme)
, an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms.
By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative is aimed to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings.
It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.
The Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).
The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.
Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of
“Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”
, the Mela is promotiong the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).
The Mela is providing a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.
In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela is creating awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations.
The initiative is complementing financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.
It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of communities having financial constraints, by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.
The Mela is enhancing the visibility of participating artisans, expanding awareness of their products and encouraging greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

content:
Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse addressed the All-Women Coaches Course under the All India Tennis Association’s (AITA) ACE 2032 initiative at the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA) Tennis Stadium in New Delhi on Saturday. She emphasised the need to expand opportunities for women across sports, from grassroots participation and coaching to high-performance competition and leadership.
The event was attended by Shri Rohit Rajpal, President, DLTA; Shri Kawaljeet Singh, Director of Coaching, AITA; Shri Ashutosh Singh, Davis Cup Coach; Shri Sunder Iyer, Honorary Secretary, AITA; Shri Dinesh Arora, Treasurer, AITA; and Coach Radhika Kanitkar, associated with the BKJC Cup. Coaches and sporting professionals also shared perspectives on strengthening coach education, grassroots tennis and athlete development.
Supported by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI), the initiative aims to strengthen the links between coach education, talent identification and high-performance training.
Expanding Women’s Participation from Grassroots to High Performance
Union MoS Raksha Khadse stressed that India’s ambition to become a leading sporting nation depends on identifying talent early and ensuring that women and girls have access to qualified coaches, suitable infrastructure, regular competition and sustained support.
She highlighted that sporting talent exists across rural, tribal, semi-urban and urban communities. Expanding participation, she noted, is vital to widening India’s talent pool and strengthening its prospects at national and international competitions. She also underlined that opportunities for women must extend beyond playing fields to coaching, sports science, administration, event management and other professional roles.
The discussions highlighted the role of ASMITA women’s leagues under the Khelo India framework in expanding access to organised sports. Launched in 2021, the leagues have reached more than three lakh women, creating opportunities for participation and competition across regions and communities.
The need to connect grassroots initiatives with Khelo India Centres, accredited academies and Centres of Excellence was also emphasised to help promising athletes progress towards higher levels of performance.
Building a Stronger Women Coaching Workforce
A key focus of the course was increasing the number of qualified women coaches and expanding access to coaching education and certification across states. Greater representation of women in coaching can help encourage girls to participate in sports while strengthening the quality and reach of athlete development.
The AITA ACE 2032 initiative seeks to connect coach education with talent identification and elite player development. Participants highlighted the importance of practical training, mentorship and continued professional development in preparing coaches for the demands of competitive sport.
Discussions also covered high-performance training and specialised coaching capabilities. Sheerika Burman, associated with high-performance training, highlighted the importance of developing expertise in this area. The programme also discussed the prospect of conducting a course in Bengaluru beginning on 10 December, with 16 players to be selected for the CHP course.
Regional Perspectives on Coaching and Player Development
Participants shared insights from their respective regions on strengthening grassroots tennis and improving coaching practices.
Preeti Srinivasan from Tamil Nadu highlighted the importance of focused coaching attention and grassroots tennis development. Marnu Riba from Arunachal Pradesh emphasised holistic player development and the importance of ensuring that athletes enjoy the sport as they build their abilities. Harjot Kaur from Jammu and Kashmir stressed the need to make Level One fitness programmes more comprehensive, particularly for beginners.
The discussions underscored the importance of coaching and fitness programmes that meet the needs of players at different stages of development and across diverse regional settings.
Creating Safe and Sustainable Careers in Sports
The course also highlighted the growing range of professional opportunities in sports, including coaching, fitness training, sports science, event management and administration. Participants stressed the need to equip more women with the skills and qualifications required to enter these fields and progress into leadership roles.
Safe sporting environments, athlete welfare and professional accountability were identified as essential to sustaining women’s participation. Coaches, sporting associations and governing bodies have a shared responsibility to uphold standards of safety, conduct and athlete protection.
The All-Women Coaches Course under AITA ACE 2032 reflects the wider effort to strengthen women’s participation and leadership in Indian sports. By expanding coaching opportunities, supporting grassroots talent and improving pathways to high-performance sport, the initiative seeks to contribute to India’s sporting ambitions for 2036 and the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

title: Viksit Bharat- G RAM G
subtitle: “Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 OCT 2026 11:56AM by PIB Delhi
content:
A New Framework for Rural Employment and Development
Aligned with the vision of
Viksit Bharat @2047
, the
Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
(
VB-G RAM G)
marks a significant reform in rural development.
The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025
came into force on
1 July 2026
and has been rolled out successfully across all rural areas of the country.
The transition from Mahatma Gandhi NREGA to VB-G RAM G has been seamless and disruption-free. Digital systems supporting implementation were operational from the commencement of the new framework.
The Act provides a statutory guarantee of
125 days of wage employment every financial year
. The guarantee covers every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. It promotes
empowerment, growth, convergence and saturation
for a prosperous and resilient rural Bharat. It focuses on four thematic areas:
water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events
.
The Act institutionalises a
Whole-of-Government approach
through convergence-driven and saturation-oriented planning. At its core is the preparation of
Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs)
. These provide an integrated framework for addressing the diverse developmental needs of Gram Panchayats.
Bottom-up Planning Envisaged through VGPPs
Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs)
are a key institutional reform under VB-G RAM G. They enable participatory, evidence-based, saturation-oriented, and convergence-driven planning at the grassroots level.
VGPPs put local needs at the centre of rural development planning. They are prepared with the active participation of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat. The Gram Sabha provides due recommendation and approval of the plans. VGPPs enable villages to identify their actual development needs, existing assets and development gaps and prioritise works accordingly.
How the VGPP Process Works
Participatory planning:
Gram Panchayats identify and prioritise works based on local needs, with the involvement of the Gram Sabha.
Asset mapping:
The process begins with a comprehensive inventory of existing assets, infrastructure and service delivery gaps within the Gram Panchayat.
Coverage of existing assets:
The inventory includes assets created under various Central and State Government schemes and programmes.
GIS-based planning:
The planning process uses GIS,
Yuktdhara, PM Gati Shakti,
and other digital tools. Geospatial and non-spatial information supports evidence-based and integrated planning based on local needs and existing assets.
Gap assessment:
Information from these platforms supports
spatial planning, better asset mapping, and avoidance of duplication
. It also helps identify infrastructure deficits, development priorities, and potential interventions.
Convergence across government:
VGPPs promote a
Whole-of-Government approach
by bringing together resources and interventions from different schemes, departments and stakeholders for integrated village development.
Multi-level consolidation:
VGPPs are consolidated at the Block, District, State and National levels. The consolidated plans contribute to the
Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack.
Permissible works:
The VGPP Framework identifies
318 types
of permissible works across the four thematic areas.
The VGPP process is intended to support integrated village development through employment-linked asset creation, improved infrastructure and convergence of public interventions.
VB G-RAM G: Progress on the Ground
As of
24 September 2026
, VB-G RAM G has recorded significant progress since its implementation on
1 July 2026
.
Active workers:
10.88 crore
in 2026-27
Assets created:
2.83 lakh
Person-days generated:
More than 31.69 crore
Women’s participation:
61.65 percent
in 2026-27
Employment provided to workers on demand:
Over 2.81 crore
belonging to
about 2.23 crore
rural households
Works under Execution:
97.17 lakh
Approved works readily available to meet future employment demand:
73.24 lakh
Active worksites operational:
Around 20.16 lakh
Number of Gram Panchayats executing works presently across the country:
Nearly 2.31 lakh
DBT transactions:
3.76 crore
in 2026-27
Wage rate: Ranges from
Rs.300 to Rs.450
per day
Total number of Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards issued:
15.17 crore
Financial Progress
A total of
Rs.
93,841 crore
has been allocated to States/UTs as interim allocation for FY 2026-27
Out of this, a Mother Sanction of
Rs.
25,880
crore
has been issued as the first instalment to the States/UTs
Technology Enabled Transparency and Governance
Technology is central to VB-G RAM G implementation
.
Digital systems support worker verification, monitoring, payments, and transparency. They also link employment with sustainable asset creation and rural development.
Digital verification:
e-KYC and worker attendance are captured through Face Authentication and biometric authentication. It significantly enhances transparency, accountability, and authenticity.
Digital work monitoring:
Geo-tagging, digital measurement, electronic Measurement Books (e-MB) and mobile-based monitoring support monitoring across different stages of implementation.
Digital payments:
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) supports payments under the framework.
Technology-enabled oversight:
Spatial technology-enabled planning, real-time dashboards, and AI-enabled analytics support monitoring, reporting, and corrective action.
Digital platforms and capacity building:
Dedicated digital platforms, citizen engagement platforms and large-scale capacity building initiatives further support implementation.
Building Rural Development from the Ground Up
VB-G RAM G brings
employment, participatory planning and rural development
together. Through VGPPs, Gram Panchayats identify local needs, map existing assets and prioritise development works. Technology, convergence and digital systems strengthen implementation, transparency and accountability. The framework links
employment with sustainable asset creation
, supporting resilient livelihoods and integrated rural development.

The three-day event ‘India Chem-2026’ which was inaugurated on 22nd October concluded in Mumbai today.
The 14th edition of India Chem 2026 held under the theme “Advantage Bharat : An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub” strengthened global partnerships, paved the way to attract investments and promote sustainable growth in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector.
During the event brainstorming sessions, business parleys and fruitful discussions were held during CEO Forum, India Japan, India-USA and India-EU Forum and roundtable talks on different challenges pertaining to Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector.
Japan, with whom India shares a robust trade relationship, particularly in the chemical and petrochemical sector, was the partner country for the event.
While inaugurating the India Chem 2026 Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, the Union Minister for Chemicals & Fertilizers and Health and Family Welfare in the august presence of the Chief Ministers of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha and Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers and Health and Family Welfare Smt. Anupriya Patel urged industry leaders, investors, innovators and policymakers of Chemicals Sector to work hand in hand to achieve the goal of ViksitBharat@2047.
Shri Nadda said Chemical and Petrochemical industry is a sunrise sector and it has huge potential to grow and contribute towards economic development.
The Union Minister said for the country to achieve the ambition of Viksit Bharat by 2047, this sector has to play an indispensable role. The sector needs to grow from its current market size of about USD 220 billion to about USD 1 trillion by 2040 and further to around USD 1.6 trillion by 2047.
The CEOs Forum presided by Shri JP Nadda focused on strengthening industry, competitiveness and advancing India’s ambition to emerge as a globally competitive chemicals and petrochemical hub.
Industry leaders from across the globe discussed the opportunities and challenges of the Indian chemical industry.
During the brainstorming sessions under India-Japan, India-US and India-EU Chemicals and Petrochemicals Forum at India Chem 2026 , representatives and industry leaders explored opportunities for deeper collaboration in trade, investment and technology related to sector.
The event held under the theme “Advantage Bharat : An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub” witnessed several roundtables like Specialty Chemicals, Infrastructure for Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Agrochemicals, Environment Issues, Plant Machinery, Pumps and Valves which are contemporary challenges for the rapid growth of the sector.
India Chem 2026 in its 14th edition witnessed a new feature “India Chem Youth Innovation Challenge” which was aligned to connect Young Innovators to the India’s Chemicals and Petrochemicals sector. It consisted of young students working on problem statements of the chemical industry and their solutions being judged by a jury of the industry. The First Prize was clinched by Soumya Bhole and Sarthak Kale, students of ICT, Mumbai. Suman Batwe and Saloni Mhadesar of VNIT, Nagpur and Jash Prasad and Smit Bambhorliya of IIT, Gandhinagar clinched second and third prizes respectively.
This event, organized jointly by the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals and FICCI, provided a platform for brainstorming discussions amongst industry leaders and Government representatives on specific topics of relevance to the sector, facilitating dialogue on investment prospects, regulatory frameworks, and strategic challenges.
The world class exhibition consisted of pavilions from leading Indian and global companies in the sector, several Indian States including partner states Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Bihar.
The event witnessed international participation from number of countries including Japan, the USA, Canada, UK, countries across the European Union, Latin America, Republic of Korea and ASEAN nations, with a footfall over more than 5000 visitors across 3 days.
